```{r reset environment and load libraries}
#Clearing the environment
rm(list = ls())

#Load Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggrepel)
library(scales)
```

```{r importing the dataset}
stat_data <- read.csv("25_26.csv")
general_data <- read.csv("25_26_Height.csv")

```

```{r}
# ---- Prepare data (run once) ----
stat_data$PLAYER <- toupper(trimws(stat_data$PLAYER))
general_data$PLAYER <- toupper(trimws(general_data$PLAYER))

df <- merge(stat_data, general_data[, c("PLAYER","HEIGHT")], by="PLAYER")

# Convert height like "7-4" to inches
df$HT <- sapply(strsplit(as.character(df$HEIGHT), "-"), function(x)
  as.numeric(x[1])*12 + as.numeric(x[2]))

df <- df[df$GP >= 20 & !is.na(df$HT), ]   # keep qualifying players
```


```{r What is the number of players that have scored 25+ points per game?}
n_elite <- sum(df$PTS >= 25)
n_rest  <- sum(df$PTS <  25)

barplot(c(n_elite, n_rest),
        names.arg = c("25+ PPG", "Under 25"),
        col = c("firebrick", "steelblue"),
        main = "Players Scoring 25+ PPG vs Under 25",
        ylab = "Number of Players")
text(c(0.7, 1.9), c(n_elite, n_rest), labels = c(n_elite, n_rest), pos = 3)

elite <- table(df$Group[df$PTS >= 25])
barplot(elite, col = "firebrick",
        main = "Where the 25+ PPG Scorers Are",
        ylab = "Number of Elite Scorers", las = 2)
```

```{r Analysis of above}
# Only a small percentage of nba players can reach 25+ Points per game, and in that small percentage the majority of players who scored that much were in the heights of 6'3-6'5 with
```


```{r Plot1}
plot(df$HT, df$PTS,
     xlab = "Height (inches)", ylab = "Points per Game",
     main = "Height vs Scoring", pch = 19, col = "steelblue")
abline(lm(PTS ~ HT, data = df), col = "red", lwd = 2)   # trend line
abline(h = 25, lty = 2)    
```

```{r Plot2}
df$Group <- cut(df$HT, breaks = c(0,72,75,78,81,84,100),
                labels = c("<6'0","6'0-6'2","6'3-6'5","6'6-6'8","6'9-6'11","7'0+"))

avg <- tapply(df$PTS, df$Group, mean)
barplot(avg, col = "steelblue",
        main = "Average PPG by Height Group",
        ylab = "Average Points", las = 2)
```

```{r Plot3}

boxplot(PTS ~ Group, data = df, col = "lightblue",
        main = "Scoring Spread by Height", ylab = "Points per Game", las = 2)
abline(h = 25, lty = 2, col = "red")
```

# Coding for What is the percentage of Players shorter than 6’5 feet? Year 24-25
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv("24_25_Height.csv")
```

```{r}
df_processed <- df %>%
  separate(HEIGHT, into = c("feet", "inches"), sep = "-", convert = TRUE, remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(HEIGHT_CM = (feet * 12 + inches) * 2.54)
```


```{r}
total_count <- nrow(df_processed)
short_count <- df_processed %>% filter(HEIGHT_CM < 195.58) %>% nrow()
percentage  <- (short_count / total_count) * 100
```

```{r}
cat("\n=== 2024-2025 NBA Season Height Analysis (CM) ===\n")
cat("Total Players in Dataset:               ", total_count, "\n")
cat("Players Shorter than 195.58 cm (6'5\"): ", short_count, "\n")
cat("Percentage Shorter than 6'5\":         ", round(percentage, 2), "%\n")
```
Analysis: 153 out of 569 players (or 26.89%) in the dataset are shorter than 6'5' (195.58 cm), according to the R script analysis for player heights. This shows that about 25% of the NBA player population under analysis is under 6'5, which is consistent with the usual roster distribution where shorter players are mostly found in backcourt guard positions.

#Coding for What is the number of players that have scored 25+ points per game? Year 24-25
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
getwd()
```

```{r}
df_2425 <- read_csv("24_25.csv")
```

```{r}
high_scorers <- df_2425 %>%
  filter(PTS >= 25)
```

```{r}
total_players <- nrow(df_2425)
count_25plus  <- nrow(high_scorers)
pct_25plus    <- (count_25plus / total_players) * 100
```

```{r}
cat("=== 2024-2025 NBA Season: 25+ PPG Analysis ===\n")
cat("Total Players Analyzed:              ", total_players, "\n")
cat("Players Scoring 25+ Points Per Game: ", count_25plus, "\n")
cat("Percentage of Players (25+ PPG):     ", round(pct_25plus, 2), "%\n\n")
```

```{r}
cat("Players with 25+ PPG:\n")
print(high_scorers %>% select(PLAYER, TEAM, PTS))
```
Analysis: 180 out of 569 players (or 31.63%) in the sample scored 25 or more points per game (PPG),
according to the R script output that was given. A crucial analytical finding, however, is that this
count seems abnormally high because of a possible data problem: top players in the output display
totals around 34–37 PPG, and standard NBA single-season scoring averages seldom feature nearly one
third of the league above 25 PPG. This suggests that the PTS column may represent total points,
normalized metrics, or fantasy values rather than actual per-game averages.
